CLASS A — PREMIUM FULL-COLOR, TUBE-BASED, HIGH OUTPUT | ETC anchor: Source Four LED Series 3 Lustr X8 (~$2,340 engine+barrel, 307W, ~11k lm, 8-color)
Closest cross-brand match in the industry. Same job, same form factor, similar money.
Higher published per-lens output (13,300 lm @26 vs ~10,900); 18-bit dimming; CRI 95.4 headline; often undercuts ETC by $300-500 in package bids; 6-color engine with mint reads very well on skin

8-color array with deep red + indigo = wider gamut and better deep saturates; XDLT optics (crisper shutter cuts, less halation); native S4 tube ecosystem the school already owns; Multiverse wireless + NFC config; 10-yr array warranty; ETC dealer/service network
A Reve E-3 is an S3 Lustr X8 with two fewer colors and no S4-tube/Multiverse/NFC ecosystem — it wins on brochure lumens, ETC wins on color depth, optics, and everything around the fixture.
Output rival, not a color rival.
15,500 engine lumens (biggest raw number in class, but measured without a tube); native Art-Net/sACN + Ethercon; dual gobo/iris slot; lighter (17.9 lb)
Color quality is a different league: Ra 93-98 vs 84-85, 8 colors vs RGBL; ETC tube ecosystem; NFC/Multiverse; established school-market pedigree
PLE+ is a brightness play with console-grade networking — but at CRI 84 it can't touch S3 color; if the spec says 'full spectrum,' it's disqualified.
Different concept: all-in-one (no tubes) with motorized-feature ambitions.
Integrated 6-50 zoom, rotating/indexing gobo slot, and built-in E-FLY wireless — one SKU does what an S4 needs tubes + accessories for; 10,600 lm total

Less than half the weight (14.9 vs 34.6 lb — big deal on old pipe grids); tube ecosystem = cheaper long-term flexibility; crisper imaging optics; cheaper; Elation has no lens-tube path if needs change
KL Profile FC is a Swiss-army ellipsoidal — great where one fixture must do everything, but it's 35 lbs and $850 more; a school rep plot is better served by S3 + tubes.
Similar output class (~10-12.8k lm); RDM-selectable fan modes
8-color vs RGBL; published CRI; lighter; Multiverse/NFC; and the big one: Altman availability/viability is in question (dealer delistings + plant-closing report)
PHX3.5 matches S3 brightness but not its color engine — and with Altman's factory status uncertain, spec'ing it is a support risk.
CLASS B — MID-POWER FULL-COLOR | ETC anchor: ColorSource Spot V (~$1,600-1,712, 199W, RGBIL, up to ~9.5k lm)
The classic head-to-head in this tier.
Slightly cheaper; convection-cooled 'silent' claim; RGBA+lime mixes warm pastels well
Notably brighter (up to 9,498 lm vs 4,316 @26); indigo emitter deepens blues; native S4 tubes (E-910FC tube fit is unofficial); Multiverse + NFC options; CRI on E-910FC is only 86
E-910FC saves ~$150 but gives up roughly half the punch and the indigo end of the gamut — Spot V is the stronger mid-tier buy.
6-in-1 RGBWAL engine (adds white+amber); 25kHz camera mode; B-size gobos; strong HoW dealer presence
Brighter; native S4 tube ecosystem vs ADJ's proprietary EP mount (locks the school into ADJ glass); RDM+Multiverse/NFC; theatrical pedigree and spare-parts path
Pro Color looks even on paper until the lens bill: its proprietary tubes lock the house into ADJ, while Spot V runs the S4 tubes they already own.
8,500 engine lumens from only 150W; selectable fan acoustics; PLT/SPX tube options
Cheaper; RGBIL gamut and TM-30 up to 106 vs Ra 84; S4 tubes; Multiverse/NFC
PLE RGBL buys raw output per watt; Spot V buys color fidelity per dollar — for theater, fidelity usually wins.
Dead-silent convection cooling (no fan at all); CRI 94
Roughly $1,000-1,600 cheaper; brighter; S4 ecosystem; availability confidence
PHX1.5 exists for rooms where zero fan noise is the spec (recital halls, broadcast) — everywhere else Spot V does more for far less.
RGBACM engine, 13.6 lb, NFC — Reve color science at mid power
Shipping today with known photometrics; Reve E2 specs still preliminary
When Reve E2 ships it likely becomes the Spot V's nearest rival — track pricing.
CLASS C — COMPACT ALL-IN-ONE ZOOM | ETC anchor: ColorSource Spot jr ($1,140-1,285, 166W, 4-color, built-in 25-50 zoom)
6-color full-spectrum (jr is 4-color); CRI 93 vs 82; ~5.6k lm flood ~= jr's output with better color; 18-bit dimming
Cheaper; lighter (12 vs 14.8 lb); ETC ecosystem/warranty (10-yr array)
E-2 FC is a jr with two more colors and camera-grade CRI for ~$250 — the honest answer is E-2 FC wins on light, jr wins on price and brand.
CRI 94.9 + TLCI 95 (best in class); RGBMA; NFC + Aria x2 wireless mgmt; dim-to-warm
~$500 cheaper; simpler for volunteer operators; ETC dealer network
KL Compact is the broadcast-grade pick; jr is the budget-grade pick — different customers.
8,500 lm field (engine-basis figure); RGBL CCT presets
Much cheaper; ZoomSpot CRI dips to 74 at some CCTs — worst color fidelity in class
Hard to justify ZoomSpot at ~1.7x the jr's price with weaker color — only the Vari-Lite house standard buys it.
Cheapest full fixture in class; 12-30 zoom; glass gobos included
RGBW COB only (no lime/indigo); no published CRI or lumens; no RDM listed; 12-30 zoom narrower than 25-50; build/support tier below
When a low bid swaps in Encore 1000s for jrs, the counter is: unpublished photometrics, RGBW-only color, and no RDM — you're not comparing like for like.

CLASS D — WHITE-LIGHT / TUNGSTEN REPLACEMENT | ETC anchor: Source 4WRD II retrofit ($692-784 into an existing S4 body). Note: ETC's only NEW white-only path is 4WRD; for new white fixtures ETC sells Series 3 Daylight HDR (tunable) instead — a gap competitors price into.
New complete fixture (no donor body); CRI 96; 10-13k lm @26; CW option
If the school owns S4s (most do), 4WRD II converts each for ~$700 and keeps every tube/accessory — half the price, zero re-rigging; dual-mode works on existing wall dimmers
'You already own the best part of the fixture' — 4WRD II turns their S4 inventory into LED for less than any new fixture; E-260WW is the answer only when there's no donor body.
Same 4WRD retrofit math as above; ADJ proprietary lens mount adds tube cost
Same story: retrofit beats replace when S4 bodies exist.
Price; retrofit math; S4 tubes native
Only competitive in a Vari-Lite-standardized house.

Whole new fixture that phase-dims like an incandescent (4 per 20A dimmer); 3000K or 5000K
4WRD II does the same dual-mode trick (phase-dim OR DMX) inside the S4 they own for a quarter of the price
PHX LVD's headline feature is one ETC already ships at $700 — lead with that.
Budget white tier below ETC's line.
Price points ETC doesn't reach with a new fixture ($890-1,177 complete)
ColorSource Spot jr (color-capable, $1,140) or 4WRD retrofit are the ETC counters; E-160WW publishes no lumen figure
If the bid is pure price-per-white-fixture, position jr's color flexibility or the 4WRD retrofit path instead of matching the number.

TIER A — FLAGSHIP / ARENA | ETC anchor: Eos Apex 5/10/20 (24K outputs unlocked, quote-only; used Apex 5 ~$44k). Reality check: this tier is rider-driven — theater riders say Eos, concert riders say MA.
The other flagship — but a different world.
Absolute standard for arena/stadium touring and broadcast spectacle (Super Bowl-class); MA-Net3 session ecosystem; motorized everything; huge rental inventory worldwide; operator pool in concerts

US theater/opera/education standard; cueing/tracking philosophy built for theater; Augment3d previz included; outputs fully unlocked (MA needs $12-33k processing units to grow past built-in parameters); ETC dealer/service network; far cheaper at equivalent capability
Eos vs MA isn't a spec fight, it's a genre fight: theater/PAC = Eos, concert touring = MA. In a school or PAC bid, Eos wins on operator availability alone — every theater student learns it.
400 universes included with zero licensing; motorized faders; built-in 3D visualizer; UPS; roughly half the money of the big two
Ecosystem and pedigree: Eos operator pool, theater feature depth, US service; ChamSys US presence is growing but thinner; rider acceptance below MA/Eos
MQ500M+ is honest capability-per-dollar, but nobody's theater rider asks for it — in Jeff's market it appears as a value alternative, counter with operator familiarity and support.
Gorgeous hardware (motorized P&G faders, optical rotaries); Synergy video integration; Robe now owns and distributes (Robe NA)
Almost no US school/theater installed base or operator pool; support network still being built via Robe NA
In WI schools an Avolites bid is exotic — flag the operator/support question and it usually self-resolves.
TIER B — MID PROFESSIONAL | ETC anchor: Ion Xe / Ion Xe 20 ($11.9k/$13.7k at 2K outputs) and Gio @5 (quote). This is the PAC/college/roadhouse tier — Jeff's core console battleground.
True MA3 (8,192 params); motorized faders; touring rider compliance; session networking

A third the price; theater cueing workflow; the operator pool in every US theater department; free offline software for training; MA3's 4,096-param onPC ceiling means the cheap MA route can't grow — the console route is $34k+
If a venue hosts national concert tours, an MA3 compact makes sense; for a PAC doing theater, dance, and rentals, Ion Xe does the job at a third the cost with operators everywhere.
The serious value threat in this tier.
MQ70: 24 universes for less than an Ion Xe 2K; LTC standard; built-in UPS + WiFi + visualizer; MQ250M adds motorized faders at $24.5k

Eos ecosystem/training/operator familiarity; ETC service; Ion upgrade path into the same software family from Element to Apex (one skillset building-wide); ChamSys learning curve is real for volunteer/student ops
MQ70 wins the spreadsheet, Ion wins the room: whoever runs the board — students, volunteers, guest LDs — already knows Eos. Standardization value beats $2k.
Value mid-size from the Elation family.
64 universes at $9.6k; NX3 (2026) adds motorized faders + NDI/CITP; often bundled when Elation fixtures win the rig
Same ecosystem argument; ONYX operator pool is small in theater; NX3 pricing unannounced
Watch for NX consoles riding in on Elation fixture packages — separate the fixture decision from the console decision in the spec.
D7 motorized faders + dual touchscreens; D3-110 is fresh 2025 hardware
Price (D7 is 2x Ion Xe); operator pool; support depth
Same story as D9 one tier down — spec-sheet strong, ecosystem weak in the US school market.
TIER C — ENTRY PROFESSIONAL / EDUCATION | ETC anchor: Element 2 ($8,420 @1K / $11,740 @6K). The high-school auditorium default — and where Peak will quote most often.
8 universes vs Element's 1K-output base tier; 8 encoders (Element 2 has none physical); WiFi + remote app included; built-in visualizer
Eos software = students learn the industry-standard; upgrade continuity to Ion/Apex; 40 physical faders (MQ50 has 10); free ETCnomad training at home; no timecode on MQ50 anyway; ETC dealer support
MQ50 gives more universes; Element 2 gives more faders and the Eos skillset colleges expect — for education that's usually decisive.
Motorized faders + 16 universes + touchscreen at $4.5k — remarkable hardware value; magnetic modular expansion
Fader count (40 vs 10); Eos pedagogy/ecosystem; ONYX is Windows-IoT-based with a smaller support bench; theater feature depth
NX1-16 is half the price and it shows up in low bids — counter on operator training, fader count for busking a musical, and long-term platform continuity.
T3 + free Titan PC is cheap and capable (16 univ)
T3 needs a host PC/touchscreen; ecosystem gap; Element is turnkey
Rare in US schools; if quoted, the 'what happens when the one person who knows Titan graduates' question lands.
TIER D — SIMPLE ONE-ROOM CONSOLES | ETC anchor: ColorSource 20/40 (+AV) ($1,992-4,476). Cafeteria/black-box/middle-school tier.
The head-to-head rival at this tier.
More universes (Q30 = 4 vs CS 1-2); WiFi + remote app standard; OSC; audio triggering; arguably slicker touchscreen workflow; MTC on Q30

CS AV models add HDMI media playback + sound-to-light (unique one-box trick for cafetoriums); RDM autopatch both ways; ETC dealer/service; Eos-family upgrade story for the district; CS20 undercuts Q10
QuickQ wins on universes and WiFi, ColorSource AV wins when the room also needs simple AV playback — ask what else the room does before quoting.
Obsidian's NX Touch is discontinued; Avolites D3 Touch is a wall panel, not a console
CS + QuickQ effectively split this tier
Two-horse race at the bottom: ETC vs ChamSys/Chauvet.
TIER E — PC/SOFTWARE + WINGS | ETC anchor: ETCnomad ($584/1K, $1,800/6K) + Puck ($3,256/$4,532) + wings. Capacity-per-dollar comparison, and each brand's training funnel.
Free onPC software; DMX-key at $956 is a cheap MA3 classroom seat; motorized wing hardware
onPC systems hard-cap at 4,096 parameters — no growth without a $34k+ console; Nomad 6K ($1,800) outguns it on capacity per dollar; Nomad key also unlocks Hog 4 PC
MA's cheap seats teach MA, but the ceiling is real; Nomad's ceiling is 6,144 outputs at $1,800 and full Eos parity.
The most generous free tier anywhere.
64 free output universes with zero hardware (2025 change) — unbeatable for a lab or previz room; Connect surfaces cheap; built-in visualizer/pixelmap/media
Eos skillset transfer to the consoles schools actually own; Nomad+wings builds a real Eos rig incrementally; MagicQ's depth comes with a steeper UI learning curve
For pure free-capacity, ChamSys wins; for teaching the console the auditorium runs, Nomad wins. Know which question the customer is asking.
Cheapest licensed universes in the industry.
8U for $599, 128U for $2,999, movable USB key; NX P motorized wing $1,999
Ecosystem/training transfer; ONYX theater feature depth thinner; 1 free universe vs MagicQ's 64
ONYX is the budget-rig champion for clubs/HoW; in schools it's a niche pick.
T1 at $489 is the cheapest name-brand PC unlock

CLASS A — PREMIUM THEATRICAL COLOR PAR | ETC anchor: Selador Desire D40/D60 (7-color x7, ~$2,080+, static, fanless, deepest gamut + high CRI). This is ETC's color-rendering flagship wash.
The closest cross-brand rival on color quality.
Cheaper; 11,000 lm (much brighter than Desire's ~2,600-4,300); CRI 92 + TLCI 95; interchangeable lenses; onboard OLED
7-color x7 gamut goes deeper on saturates than KL's 5-color RGBMA; fanless-silent (KL runs a fan); ETC theatrical pedigree, rep-plot familiarity, and the Selador color-matching designers know

KL PAR FC wins brightness and price; Desire wins gamut depth and silence. For a color-critical theatrical wash where designers spec Selador by name, Desire holds; for punch-per-dollar, KL is hard to beat.
Brighter, IP, but a different mission.
~10,000 lm and IP65 (Desire is neither bright nor weatherproof); RGBAM full-spectrum mint engine reads white/skin well
Deeper theatrical gamut; fanless silence; lighter; the Selador name; ETC ecosystem
Reve P-3 IP is the answer when the wash goes outdoors or needs big output; indoors, for color depth and silence, Desire still wins its niche.
Motorized zoom (Desire is fixed-lens); RGBW; event-friendly
RGBW at TM-30 Rf 60 is nowhere near Selador color rendering; Desire is a theatrical instrument, PROPAR is an event par
Different tools — if someone cross-shops these, they've mis-scoped the job.
CLASS B — MID FULL-COLOR WASH PAR | ETC anchor: ColorSource PAR / PAR Deep Blue (RGB-L, $876, static, interchangeable-lens). The school/HoW/small-theater workhorse — Peak's most-quoted PAR.
RGBAL (5-color, adds amber) with published CRI 87.9; more lens options (12.8/23.2/73.2); silent convection

Native ETC ecosystem (matches Eos rigs & ColorSource consoles); indigo Deep Blue variant for cyc color; simpler for volunteer ops; strong ETC dealer support and the ColorSource family story from console to fixture
P-56FC has a richer engine on paper; ColorSource PAR wins on ETC-system fit, the Deep Blue option, and support — for an ETC-standardized building it's the coherent choice.
More capable, at a price/complexity step up.
IP65 (ColorSource PAR is indoor-only); CRI 94.9; RGBMA; Aria wireless; tunable-white presets
Cheaper; lighter; simpler; ETC ecosystem; ColorSource is the known quantity for school TDs
If the wash ever goes outside or needs high CRI, KL PAR IP Compact earns the premium; for a dry stage on an ETC rig, ColorSource PAR is the value pick.
ADJ Encore LP12 IP / Vari-Lite EventPAR RGBA
Encore LP12 IP is cheaper AND IP65 with lime engine; EventPAR RGBA adds manual zoom + finishes

ColorSource sits between them on price with the ETC-system coherence and Deep Blue option; Encore's proprietary nature and ADJ support tier are the trade; EventPAR is an event/install look, not a rep-plot wash
Encore LP12 IP is the low-bid threat (cheaper and IP) — counter with ETC ecosystem and the fact that a dry stage doesn't need IP65; you're paying for weatherproofing you won't use.
CLASS C — COMPACT / BUDGET COLOR PAR | ETC anchor: ColorSource PAR jr (RGB-L, $540, fanless, small). Cafeteria/black-box/uplight-on-a-budget.
6-color RGBAW+UV hex (adds amber + UV for saturated uplight & effects); cheaper (12PX) or similar (18P); RF remote option
ETC color calibration & no-red-shift dimming; RGB-L renders theatrical color better than hex saturation does; ETC support and the Deep Blue jr option; fanless silence
For pure saturated uplight on a tight budget, HEX pars win the spreadsheet; for a wash that has to render stage color and match an ETC rig, PAR jr is the right tool even at a small premium.
Chauvet COLORdash PAR H7X / Elation SIX+ PAR S
Hex / 6-color+UV engines with published lumens (H7X 2,738 lm); IP options in the family
ETC ecosystem, calibrated color, silence, price at the bottom of the range
Same story as ADJ hex — engine count isn't the same as color quality; match to whether it's uplight punch or stage rendering.

CLASS D — IP MOTORIZED-ZOOM EVENT / TOURING PAR | *** ETC HAS NO ENTRY *** This whole class (Chauvet COLORado Solo/Quad zoom, Elation Limelight, ADJ Encore LP12Z IP, Vari-Lite PROPAR, Altman AIP-200) is a category ETC does not build. Know the gap and don't try to force a ColorSource PAR into a rental/event/architainment zoom-wash spec.
Chauvet COLORado 2 Solo (~$1,197), Elation Limelight, ADJ Encore LP12Z IP ($1,150), VL800 PROPAR

IP65 + motorized zoom + event durability — the standard for rental, touring, architainment, and outdoor uplight. ADJ Encore LP12Z IP is the value leader; Chauvet Solo/Quad is the rental default; Limelight is the punch option
Nothing — ETC's answer is 'we don't make this; here's a Desire/ColorSource for the theatrical wash, and we'd partner or spec a Chauvet/Elation for the event-zoom-par need'

When a bid needs IP zoom pars, don't fake it with ETC — either concede the line item or, since Peak carries multiple lines, quote the right event par (Chauvet/Elation/ADJ) alongside the ETC theatrical package. Honesty here protects the ETC pull-through everywhere else.

CLASS E — WHITE / TUNABLE-WHITE PAR | ETC anchor: none purpose-built (ETC's white-PAR answer is a Selador Desire Studio array or a ColorSource PAR run at white). Competitors sell dedicated white pars.
(Desire Studio array / CS PAR at white)
Vari-Lite EventPAR WW ($1,899, CRI>97, 10,251 lm), ADJ Par Z100 ($430), Chauvet COLORado VW
ETC covers this with color fixtures, not a dedicated white par.
Dedicated high-CRI white output: EventPAR WW is 97 CRI and very bright; Par Z100 is a cheap single-color zoom; Chauvet VW is tunable
A Desire Studio or ColorSource PAR gives white AND color from one inventory (buy once, use for wash or white); dedicated white pars are single-purpose
If the customer only needs white, a dedicated white par is cheaper per lumen; if they want flexibility, ETC's color fixtures double as white and simplify inventory.
CLASS U — UV / EFFECT | *** ETC HAS NO ENTRY *** Chauvet Ovation P-56UV (true 365nm) owns this. If a bid needs blacklight, quote the Chauvet — ETC doesn't make one.
Dedicated cyc/wash (no asym. reflector; wide even optics)
Cyc lens ADAPTER — converts an S4 LED engine into a cyc
Host engine (x7 / Lustr X8 / Daylight HDR)
IP batten — cyc / footlight / downlight (CYC diffusion filter)
IP batten — uplight / wall-cyc wash (glare shield incl.)
Dedicated cyc — patented asymmetric reflector; top/floor
Batten used for cyc/backdrop (symmetric, NOT dedicated cyc)
* ETC ColorSource CYC / Linear / S4 LED CYC adapter are indoor/dry-location (no published IP rating); treated as IP20-class.

CLASS A — PREMIUM HIGH-CRI DEDICATED CYC | *** ETC HAS NO DIRECT MATCH *** ETC's ColorSource CYC is a mid-tier unit; there's no premium high-CRI ETC cyc to answer Elation KL Cyc L (CRI 96.5) or Vari-Lite Coda (CRI 94). For color-critical broadcast/theatre cyc, ETC's honest play is a Selador/S4 LED wash into the cyc, not a dedicated unit.
CRI 96.5, true asymmetric reflector, 9,249 lm, RGBMA 2400-8500K tunable — the color-critical studio/theatre cyc standard
Nothing dedicated — ETC would answer with S4 LED (Lustr X8) + CYC adapter to get high-CRI x8 color into the cyc, leveraging existing inventory and console family
When the spec demands broadcast-grade cyc color, don't force a ColorSource CYC — either concede to KL Cyc, or pitch S4 LED engines + CYC adapters if the house owns them (x8 color, one family).
~13,000 lm, RGBALC 6-color, CRI 94, fanless silent, 1800-10,000K — flagship broadcast cyc
No ETC dedicated equal; S4 LED + CYC adapter is the ecosystem answer for ETC houses
Coda is the premium ceiling of the category — ETC competes on ecosystem/retrofit, not head-to-head cyc hardware.

CLASS B — MID DEDICATED CYC | ETC anchor: ColorSource CYC (~$1,760, 4,117 lm, RGBI-L). This is where the real fight is — and where ETC is genuinely outgunned on paper. Sell the two ETC plays (retrofit adapter, ecosystem+indigo), not the spec sheet.
The uncomfortable one: cheaper and brighter.
